If commercial interests guided Venice, the state in turn regulated its citizens' commercial activity. "The Venetian travelling to the Levant on business," remarks Daniel Waley,

was likely to go in a state-built galley, commanded by a captain chosen by the state, within a convoy organised by the state, and when he reached Alexandria or Acre he might well be ordered to join other Venetians in a joint, state-organised purchase of cotton or pepper. The advantage of the last system was that prices would be kept lower if Venetians were not competing against each other. The convoy system for longer voyages goes back at least to the twelfth century. By the thirteenth the routine arrangements allowed for two convoys of galleys a year to the eastern Mediterranean and by the beginning of the fourteenth there were also annual sailings to England and Flanders, to north Africa ("Barbary") and to Aigues-Mortes (near the mouth of the Rhone). The arsenal, the state shipbuilding yard, dates back to the early thirteenth century and the materials used there were usually purchased directly by the Venetian republic.
国家作为资产阶级的执行委员会，认真对待自己的职责。
The state, executive committee of the bourgeoisie, took its responsibilities seriously.

然而，威尼斯的国家机构从来都不庞大。其财政体系适合精简的政府。例如，1184年，威尼斯对基奥贾潟湖所产盐的生产和销售建立了垄断；尽管这种垄断鼓励了小规模走私和欺诈，它也在无需大量人力的情况下产生了可观的收入。自13世纪起，公社确立了有固定偿付来源的公债。代表这种公债的证券——旧公债（Monte Vecchio）及其后继的其他公债（Monti）——成为威尼斯及其他地方受人青睐的投资对象。该城借款以筹措战争经费，然后依靠关税和消费税来偿还。大型礼仪与慈善兄弟会（Scuole Grandi）向国家贷出了大笔款项（Pullan 1971: 138）。由于它可以从自己的商人那里借款，并从一个高度商业化的经济中对流通征税，国家几乎不必为其财政创设什么新组织。

Yet the Venetian state was never bulky. The fiscal system lent itself to slim government. In 1184, for example, Venice established a monopoly over the production and sale of salt from Chioggia's lagoon; although such a monopoly encouraged petty smuggling and fraud, it also produced substantial revenues without extensive manpower. From the thirteenth century onward, the commune established a funded debt. The Monte Vecchio and the other Monti succeeding it, the securities representing that debt, came to be a favorite investment in Venice and elsewhere. The city borrowed to finance wars, then relied on customs and excise to pay for them. The great ritual and charitable confraternities, the Scuole Grandi, loaned substantial sums to the state (Pullan 1971: 138). Since it could borrow from its own merchants and tax the flows through an extensively commercialized economy, the state created little new organization for its finances.

14世纪使威尼斯更突出地卷入陆战，国家结构也相应地发展起来。随着北意大利的城邦开始扩张其领土，它们既威胁到威尼斯在大陆上的工业原料来源，也威胁到其商人通往跨越阿尔卑斯山的重要贸易路线的通道。威尼斯人开始了两种命运攸关的游戏：在大陆上征服，以及与其他北意大利强国变换联盟。到该世纪末，随着阿尔卑斯山以北的列强开始认真侵入北意大利，威尼斯组织起反法联盟，并与卡斯蒂利亚国王和德意志皇帝之类的强国联合。一批常驻使节被派往欧洲各大宫廷。与此同时，土耳其人沿东地中海乃至深入意大利的推进，使该城卷入日益增多的海战。

The fourteenth century involved Venice more emphatically in land warfare, and built up the state structure correspondingly. As the city-states of northern Italy began to expand their territories, they threatened both Venice's sources of industrial supplies on the mainland and its merchants' access to vital trade routes across the Alps. Venetians began two fateful games: conquest on the mainland, and shifting alliances with other north Italian powers. By the end of the century, as transalpine powers started serious incursions into northern Italy, Venice was organizing coalitions against France, and joining with such powers as the king of Castile and the German emperor. A set of permanent ambassadors fanned out to the major courts of Europe. The advance of the Turks around the eastern Mediterranean, and even into Italy, simultaneously drew the city into increased naval warfare.

战争规模的扩大引起了该城战争组织的改变。威尼斯第一次把战争委托给外人，即雇佣兵队长（condottieri），他们雇用大量雇佣兵。政府则派出贵族专员（provveditori）来平衡雇佣兵队长的影响，这些专员在补给、薪酬、有时甚至军事战略本身方面拥有广泛的权力（Hale 1979）。不久之后，该城在其属地和威尼斯本土实行征兵，工匠行会和店主行会分得为战船配备桨手的配额。在15世纪，威尼斯开始强迫罪犯和俘虏为其桨帆船划桨；在这一过程中，桨帆船从三列桨战船——每排需要三名熟练桨手、每人一支桨——转变为每排一支大桨的船，即便是没有技能、不情愿、戴着镣铐的囚犯也能靠体重来划动。全志愿兵的时代早已过去。
The expanded scale of warfare caused changes in the city's organization for war. For the first time, Venice entrusted warfare to outsiders,
condottieri,
who employed mercenaries in large numbers. The government balanced
condottiere
influence by sending out patrician commissioners,
provveditori,

who had widespread power over supplies, pay, and sometimes military strategy itself (Hale 1979). Not long after, the city resorted to conscription in its subject territories and in Venice itself, where the guilds of artisans and shopkeepers received quotas of oarsmen for war galleys. During the fifteenth century, Venice began to force convicts and captives to man its galleys; in the process, the galleys shifted from the trireme, which required three skilled rowers, each with his own oar, on every bench, to the ship with one large oar per bench, on which even unskilled, reluctant, and shackled prisoners could lean their weight. The day of an all-volunteer force had long since passed.

战争的膨胀和脱离公民兵的转变给该城带来了新的财政负担。到14世纪后期，威尼斯为偿付战争引发的债务而征收强制借款、所得税和直接财产税。然而，这些非常措施并没有建立起庞大或常设的官僚机构；在一个高度商业化的经济中，选举产生的官员和一支由文书与秘书组成的小型专业队伍，在没有大批人员的情况下管理着该城的账目。国家把许多责任分摊给公民，例如要求这些大型兄弟会自行装备战争舰队的一部分（Pullan 1971: 147-56; Lane 1973b: 163）。财政义务也没有压垮该城的财政机构。在17世纪初，当其他欧洲国家正痛苦地累积战争债务时，威尼斯竟然设法暂时清偿了其全部长期债务（Lane 1973a: 326）。

The swelling of warfare and the shift away from citizen-soldiers placed new financial burdens on the city. By the later fourteenth century, Venice was levying forced loans, income taxes, and direct property taxes to pay its war-induced debts. Nevertheless, these exceptional efforts did not build up a bulky or permanent bureaucracy; in a highly commercialized economy, elected officials and a small professional corps of clerks and secretaries administered the city's accounts without a large staff. The state parceled out many responsibilities to the citizenry, as when they required the Scuole Grandi to raise portions of a war fleet on their own (Pullan 1971: 147-56; Lane 1973b: 163). Nor did financial obligations overwhelm the city's fiscal apparatus. At the start of the seventeenth century, while other European states were painfully accumulating war debts, Venice actually managed temporarily to liquidate its entire long-term indebtedness (Lane 1973a: 326).

早在1600年之前，该城就已越过了其商业权力的顶点。自15世纪起，一连串变化把威尼斯降为国际舞台上的二流角色：土耳其把威尼斯排除在黑海和东地中海港口之外；威尼斯领土几乎被哈布斯堡、波旁和土耳其帝国所包围；威尼斯获取木材的渠道日渐萎缩，其造船业因而衰败；它控制达尔马提亚的能力不断减弱；以及荷兰和英格兰等大西洋海上强国的地中海竞争兼海盗活动。通过绕航非洲并渗入印度洋的贸易路线，葡萄牙商人打破了威尼斯对香料贸易的扼制。在16世纪末，葡萄牙船只运载着欧洲人从远东带回的全部香料和药材的四分之一到一半（Steensgard 1981: 131）。然而，葡萄牙的支配并未持续多久；一个世纪之内，组织高效的荷兰和英国东印度公司便取代了它们的伊比利亚对手（Steensgard 1974）。

Well before 1600, the city passed its apogee of commercial power. From the fifteenth century onward, a concatenation of changes reduced Venice to a second-rank actor on the international scene: Turkey's exclusion of Venice from Black Sea and eastern Mediterranean ports, the near-surrounding of Venetian territory by Habsburg, Bourbon, and Turkish empires, Venice's declining access to timber, its consequently dwindling shipbuilding industry, its diminishing ability to control Dalmatia, and Mediterranean competition-cum-piracy of Atlantic maritime powers such as Holland and England. By circumnavigating Africa and penetrating the Indian Ocean's trade routes, Portuguese merchants broke the Venetian stranglehold on the spice trade. At the end of the sixteenth century, Portuguese vessels were carrying from a quarter to a half of all the spices and drugs that Europeans brought from the Far East (Steensgard 1981: 131). Portuguese dominance did not last long, however; within a century the efficiently-organized Dutch and British East India Companies had displaced their Iberian rivals (Steensgard 1974).
大型武装帆船在地中海的登场，打破了威尼斯桨帆船的长期霸权。此后威尼斯依然繁忙而独立，越来越多地从事制造业和管理其大陆领土，但不再是地中海的主导力量。即便在曾经几乎成为该城私有的亚得里亚海内，16世纪的威尼斯船只也无法遏制拉古萨的竞争商人，或制止海盗的劫掠。在18世纪，他们放弃了把外国军舰逐出其海湾的努力。到那时，积极参与亚得里亚海贸易竞争的已不只是拉古萨，还有的里雅斯特和安科纳。

The arrival of the large, armed sailing ship on the Mediterranean scene cracked the long hegemony of the Venetian galley. Thereafter Venice remained bustling and independent, increasingly engaged in manufacturing and in administration of its mainland territory, but no longer the Mediterranean's leading force. Even within the Adriatic, once practically the city's private lake, sixteenth-century Venetian vessels were unable to contain the rival merchants of Ragusa or to check the depredations of pirates. In the eighteenth century, they gave up trying to exclude foreign warships from their gulf. By then, not only Ragusa but also Trieste and Ancona competed actively for Adriatic trade.

威尼斯满足于一种军事和外交上中立的总政策、一个重要的商业生态位、日益依赖大陆领土作为经济基础，以及由旧寡头集团支配的共和式公共生活。阿尔贝托·特嫩蒂（Alberto Tenenti）就17世纪总结道，“在政治独立与商业成功之间的艰难抉择中，在对自身命运的犹疑之中，威尼斯自豪的决心依然在她的种种错误和不光彩举动之上熠熠生辉。这座古老的城邦没有像其邻邦拉古萨那样选择一种没有风险、也没有历史的生活，而是拒绝向任何强权的支配让路，无论那是土耳其的还是教皇的，西班牙的还是哈布斯堡的”（Tenenti 1967: xvii-xviii）。

Venice settled for a general policy of military and diplomatic neutrality, an important commercial niche, an increasing reliance on mainland territories as an economic base, and a republican public life dominated by the old oligarchy. "In the hard choice between political independence and commercial success," concludes Alberto Tenenti about the seventeenth century, "in her uncertainty about her own fate, the proud determination of Venice still shone forth above all her mistaken and her shabby actions. Instead of choosing, like her neighbor Ragusa, a life with no risks and no history, the old city-state refused to give way to the predominance of any power, be it Turkish or Papal, Spanish or Habsburg" (Tenenti 1967: xvii-xviii).
然而这一选择最终失败了：1797年，拿破仑的入侵终结了18世纪的格局。威尼斯及其大陆领土先成为奥地利的财产，随后成为拿破仑治下的意大利王国的财产，然后又回到奥地利手中。1848年，达尼埃莱·马宁领导的一批起义者短暂掌权，但奥地利很快使其革命臣民就范。最后，在1866年，普鲁士对奥地利的胜利使威尼斯得以加入新的意大利民族国家。

Yet that choice finally failed: in 1797, Napoleon's invasion brought the eighteenth-century settlement to an end. Venice and its mainland territories became properties first of Austria, then of a Napoleonic kingdom of Italy, then again of Austria. In 1848, a group of insurgents led by Daniele Manin briefly held power, but Austria soon brought its revolutionary subjects into line. Finally, in 1866, Prussia's defeat of Austria freed Venice to join the new Italian national state.

威尼斯走的是一条独特的历史轨迹。然而，该城的历史与热那亚、拉古萨、米兰、佛罗伦萨，甚至与荷兰、加泰罗尼亚或汉萨都有某些共同之处。毕竟，在14世纪，巴塞罗那曾派商人往来于地中海各地，并统治着底比斯、雅典和比雷埃夫斯。荷兰共和国这个时常动荡的贸易中心联邦，在一个多世纪里一直是欧洲占主导地位的国家之一。城邦、城市帝国和城市联邦都曾作为商业和政治强国各自维持数百年之久，把商业目标置于高度优先的地位，在没有庞大官僚机构的情况下创造出有效的国家结构，发明了相对高效的支付战争和其他国家开支的方式，并把代表其商业寡头集团的机构构建进国家的组织本身。

Venice followed a unique historical trajectory. Yet the city's history had something in common with Genoa, Ragusa, Milan, Florence, and even Holland, Catalonia, or the Hanse. During the fourteenth century, after all, Barcelona sent traders up and down the Mediterranean, and ruled Thebes, Athens, and Piraeus. The Dutch Republic, a frequently turbulent federation of trading centers, remained one of Europe's dominant states for more than a century. City-states, city-empires, and urban federations all held their own for centuries as commercial and political powers, gave high priority to commercial objectives, created effective state structures without large bureaucracies, invented relatively efficient ways of paying for war and other state expenditures, and built institutions representing their commercial oligarchies into the very organization of their states.

资本密集型国家形成在三个根本方面不同于强制密集型和资本化强制的变革路径。（1）商业寡头集团的影响促进了以保护和扩展商业事业——在欧洲的经验中尤其是海运事业——为组织轴心的国家的发展。（2）资产阶级为捍卫自身利益而创设的制度，实际上有时成为国家行政的工具；威尼斯、热那亚和荷兰共和国实现了市政政府与国家政府的非凡融合。（3）资本和资本家的可得性，使这些国家能够有效地借款、征税、购买和进行战争，而无需建立庞大、持久的国家行政机构。直到以本国征募的陆军和海军进行的战争的规模本身，压倒了它们高效而紧凑的军事力量之前，资本密集型国家在一个好战的世界中繁荣兴旺。在美第奇借助教皇军队重返其故乡佛罗伦萨进行统治之后不久，尼科洛·马基雅维里写道：

如果有人在绅士众多的国家里想要建立一个共和国，他若不把他们全部消灭就无法成功；而谁若想在自由和平等盛行的地方建立一个王国或公国，也同样会失败，除非他把一些最为大胆、最有野心的人物从那种普遍的平等中拉出来，使他们成为真正的而不只是名义上的绅士，办法是给予他们城堡和产业，以及金钱和臣民；这样一来，被这些人环绕，他便能维持自己的权力，而他们靠他的支持可以满足自己的野心，其余的人则被迫屈服于那个只有武力才能使他们屈服的枷锁。
（《论李维》，I，55；这条恰当的引文承蒙理查德·弗兰克提示）

Capital-intensive state formation differed from coercion-intensive and capitalized-coercion paths of change in three fundamental regards. (1) The influence of commercial oligarchies promoted the development of states organized around the protection and expansion of commercial enterprise - especially, in European experience, maritime enterprise. (2) The institutions created by the bourgeoisie for the defense of their own interests actually became sometime instruments of state administration; Venice, Genoa, and the Dutch Republic achieved a remarkable fusion of municipal and national government. (3) The availability of capital and capitalists permitted these states to borrow, tax, purchase, and wage war effectively without creating bulky, durable national administrations. Until the sheer scale of war with nationally recruited armies and navies overwhelmed their efficient but compact military power, capital-intensive states prospered in a warlike world. Not long after the Medici, with the aid of papal armies, returned to rule his native Florence, Niccolò Machiavelli wrote that

if any one should wish to establish a republic in a country where there are many gentlemen, he will not succeed until he has destroyed them all; and whoever desires to establish a kingdom or principality where liberty and equality prevail, will equally fail, unless he withdraws from that general equality a number of the boldest and most ambitious spirits, and makes gentlemen of them, not merely in name but in fact, by giving to them castles and possessions, as well as money and subjects; so that surrounded by these he may be able to maintain his power, and that by his support they may satisfy their ambition, and the others may be constrained to submit to that yoke to which force alone has been able to subject them.
Discourses
, I, 55; I owe this apt reference to Richard Frank)
最重要的是，绅士——也就是贵族地主——支撑着强制密集型国家，而资本家——也就是商人、银行家和制造商——支配着作为其对手的资本密集型国家。二者经历上的差异，取决于它们形成的时间、它们试图控制的领土有多大、农业和制造业在多大程度上成为其经济基础的重要部分，以及它们专营何种商品。

More than anything else, gentlemen -that is, aristocratic landlords - shouldered coercion-intensive states, while capitalists -that is, merchants, bankers, and manufacturers - dominated their capital-intensive rivals. The differences in their experiences depended on when they formed, how much territory they attempted to control, the extent to which agriculture and manufacturing became significant parts of their economic bases, and in what kinds of commodities they specialized.
这些因素反过来又取决于每个国家核心城市的地理和地缘政治位置。大片农业腹地的存在（在它出现的地方）促进了更大的领土国家的形成。主要充当长途贸易市场的港口城市，更经常地以小片本土领土为基础创建城邦或城市帝国。与有实力的帝国和民族国家相邻，则有利于要么被并入那些国家，要么加入同样争夺领土控制的斗争。不过，这些变异都是在资本和资本家强大存在所设定的限度之内运作的。

These factors depended, in their turn, on the geographic and geopolitical locations of the core cities in each state. The presence of large agricultural hinterlands, when it occurred, promoted the formation of larger territorial states. Port cities serving primarily as markets for long-distance trade more frequently created city-states or city-empires on the basis of small home territories. Adjacency to substantial empires and national states favored either absorption into those states or entry into the same struggle for control of territory. These variations, nevertheless, operated within limits set by the powerful presence of capital and capitalists.

显然，并非整个上亚得里亚海都同样好地展示了经由国家形成的资本型路径。奥地利最终设法取得了包括的里雅斯特在内的一大段海岸，并使之从属于一个在别处有强烈强制利益的国家。拜占庭、塞尔维亚、匈牙利和奥斯曼帝国都曾与威尼斯争夺对达尔马提亚的控制，而奥斯曼人赢了——至少赢了好几个世纪。然而，上亚得里亚海的历史与欧洲俄罗斯的历史形成了鲜明对照。在亚得里亚海，充裕的资本促进了武装力量尤其是海上力量的建设，但也为资本家抵制建立那种能把他们的利益从属于某个王朝利益的大国，提供了诱因和手段。在俄罗斯，集中资本的稀少（尤其是在14世纪与亚洲和拜占庭帝国的贸易联系收缩之后）以及武士地主的存在，使所有形成的国家都倾向于采用强制手段。在那里，重大问题是大贵族们是否会继续把碎裂的主权握在许多只手中，还是某一位统治者会设法对所有其余的人确立牢固的优先地位。一旦俄罗斯国家选择了集中建设武装力量，其努力便造就了一个笨重的国家：在这个国家里，地主在其自己的领地内保有极大的裁量权，但在面对沙皇时却失去了这种权力。

Not all of the upper Adriatic, obviously, illustrates the capitalist path through state formation equally well. Austria eventually managed to claim a significant section of the shore, including Trieste, and to subordinate it to a state that had strong coercive interests elsewhere. Byzantine, Serbian, Hungarian, and Ottoman empires all struggled with Venice for control of Dalmatia, and the Ottomans won -at least for several centuries. Nevertheless, the upper Adriatic's history contrasts sharply with that of European Russia. In the Adriatic, abundant capital facilitated the building of armed force, especially maritime force, but provided an incentive and a means for capitalists' resistance to the creation of large states that could subordinate their interests to those of a dynasty. In Russia, the rarity of concentrated capital (especially after the fourteenth-century contraction of trade connections with Asia and the Byzantine Empire) and the presence of warrior-landlords predisposed all the states that formed toward coercive means. There the big question was whether magnates would continue to hold fragmented sovereignty in their many hands, or a single ruler would somehow establish firm priority over all the rest. Once the Russian state opted for the centralized construction of armed force, its efforts brought into being a ponderous state in which landlords retained great discretion within their own territories, but lost it vis-a-vis the tsar.

农民的命运——在18世纪以前几乎欧洲各地人口的主体——在强制密集型地区和资本密集型地区之间截然不同。在强制密集型国家形成的大多数地区，统治者与保有广泛军事和民事权力的大地主密切合作创建国家。俄罗斯、波兰、匈牙利和勃兰登堡-普鲁士是这一过程的范例，该过程在西西里和卡斯蒂利亚也有一些平行之处。在这样的国家里，16世纪贸易的扩张鼓励并使得地主在国家权力的支持下，把此前曾从其身上获取充裕地租的农民变为农奴；最常见的是，他们要求耕种者家户在领主自营地上从事报酬微薄的劳役，而这些家户靠法律把他们束缚于其上的小块农场维持自身生计。在其他强制密集型地区（尤其是斯堪的纳维亚），地主从未取得其东欧同类那样的经济和政治权力，16世纪及以后的统治者便借助教士和其他官僚对农民实行直接控制，从而保证了以自给为导向的农民的长期存续。

The fate of peasants - the bulk of the population almost everywhere in Europe before the eighteenth century -differed dramatically between coercion-intensive and capital-intensive regions. In most areas of coercion-intensive state formation, rulers created states in close collaboration with large landlords who retained extensive military and civilian powers. Russia, Poland, Hungary, and Brandenburg-Prussia exemplify the process, which had some parallels in Sicily and Castile. In such states, the expansion of trade in the sixteenth century encouraged and enabled landlords, backed by state power, to enserf peasants from whom they had previously drawn ample rents; most commonly, they required poorly-remunerated labor service on the landlord's demesne from cultivator households who drew their own subsistence from small farms to which they were attached by law. In other coercion-intensive regions (especially Scandinavia) where landlords never acquired the economic and political power of their eastern European counterparts, rulers of the sixteenth century and later instituted direct controls over the peasantry with the help of clergy and other bureaucrats, thus guaranteeing the long survival of subsistence-oriented peasants.

在资本密集型地区，如尼德兰和瑞士的部分地区，农民发生了分化。在城市市场和进取心强的资本家在场的情况下，农业很早就商业化了，并常常与乡村工业相结合。结果，少数农民靠经济作物和邻人的劳动致富。多数人则成为贫穷的雇工，其中许多人在需求上升时兼做家庭制造业或小贩营生。在无处不在的商人的伴随下，少数人和多数人共同造就了一种乡村经济：它轻易地供养其城市，易于进行有效征税，并落入作为区域贸易中心的城市的控制之下。农民的这些彼此对照的经历，既是资本密集型地区与强制密集型地区国家形成轨迹大不相同的原因，也是其结果。

In capital-intensive areas, such as the Netherlands and some of Switzerland, the peasantry underwent bifurcation. In the presence of urban markets and aggressive capitalists, agriculture commercialized early and frequently combined with rural industry. As a result, a minority of peasants grew rich on cash crops and the labor of their neighbors. The majority became poor wage-laborers, many of whom doubled in domestic manufacturing or peddling when demand was on the upswing. In the company of omnipresent merchants, the minority and the majority produced a rural economy that supplied its cities easily, lent itself to efficient taxation, and fell under the control of cities that were regional centers of trade. Contrasting peasant experiences were both cause and effect of the very different trajectories of state formation in capital-intensive and coercion-intensive regions.

在资本型与强制型两个极端之间，是资本化强制的诸路径，即强制集中与资本集中以更大程度的均等、更紧密的相互联系而出现的那些情形。不列颠群岛——爱尔兰、苏格兰、英格兰和威尔士——展示了这条路径。它们还表明，任何经验在强制—资本图中的位置，在多大程度上取决于我们为该经验所设定的时间与地理界限。从公元990年的丹麦来看，不列颠群岛像是以斯堪的纳维亚为中心的庞大帝国中的一个征服与贡赋的边缘地带。若从爱尔兰出发审视此后整个时期，不列颠群岛的国家形成比从英格兰东南部来看带有远为浓厚的强制色彩。从1500年至1700年这一时段的苏格兰来看，国家形成看起来是三个经济基础各异、颇为独立的国家——英格兰、爱尔兰和苏格兰——之间的竞争与互动。因此，应当明确：我们所考察的是公元900年之后一千年间的整个地区。在整个千年之中，中心剧情是一个最初在征服中形成、但很快被一个巨大港口和一种商业化经济所制衡的英格兰国家的扩张。

In between the capitalist and coercive extremes lay the paths of capitalized coercion, those instances where the concentrations of coercion and of capital occurred in greater equality and tighter connection with each other. The British Isles - Ireland, Scotland, England, and Wales - illustrate the path. They also show how much the placement of any experience within the coercion-capital diagram depends on the temporal and geographic limits we place on the experience. Seen from Denmark in the year 990, the British Isles look like a peripheral zone of conquest and tribute within a substantial empire centered on Scandinavia. Seen from Ireland over the period since then, state formation in the British Isles has a much more coercive cast than when seen from southeastern England. Seen from Scotland over the years 1500 to 1700, state formation looks like the competition and interaction of three rather separate states having different economic bases - English, Irish, and Scottish. Let it be clear, then, that we are examining the whole region during the thousand years following AD 900. Over the whole millennium the central drama was the expansion of an English state initially formed in conquest but soon counterbalanced by a great port and a commercialized economy.
在公元990年，爱尔兰陷于多个凯尔特王国与北欧人在沿海的领地之间的斗争之中。尽管多个北欧征服者瓜分了北海的岛屿，苏格兰和威尔士本土却在武士国王的领导下或多或少统一了起来。丹麦人克努特正在从盎格鲁-撒克逊国王埃塞尔雷德手中夺取一个联系松散的英格兰，而后者已经向丹麦人缴纳了十年贡赋。不仅缴纳贡赋，还不断遭受劫掠。在997年的条目中，《劳德编年史》记载道：

In the year 990, Ireland was locked in struggle among multiple Celtic kingdoms and the coastal dominions of Norsemen. Although multiple Nordic conquerors divided the islands of the North Sea, mainland Scotland and Wales were more or less unified under the leadership of warrior-kings. A Dane, Canute, was in the process of wresting a weakly-connected England from Anglo-Saxon King Ethelred, who had already paid tribute to the Danes for a decade. Not only paid tribute, but suffered continual depredation. In its entry for 997, the Laud Chronicle reports that:
这一年，［丹麦］军队绕过德文郡进入塞文河口，在康沃尔、威尔士和德文郡一带劫掠，并在瓦切特登陆；他们焚烧杀戮，造成极大破坏，然后绕过兰兹角回到南侧，进入塔玛河口，溯河而上直至利德福德。他们在那里焚烧并杀害所遇到的一切，把塔维斯托克的奥德伍尔修道院教堂烧成平地，带着无法形容的大量战利品回到船上。（Garmonsway 1953: 131）

In this year the [Danish] host went around Devonshire into the mouth of the Severn, and there harried, both in Cornwall, Wales, and Devon, and landed at Watchet; they wrought great havoc by burning and killing people and went back round Land's End to the south side, and entered the estuary of the Tamar, and so up it until they came to Lydford. There they burned and slew everything they met, and burnt to the ground Ordwul's abbey church at Tavistock, carrying off an indescribable amount of plunder with them to the ships. (Garmonsway 1953: 131)

当其他斯堪的纳维亚人航行到冰岛、格陵兰和美洲时，克努特及其劫掠者暂时把英格兰纳入了一个一直延伸到丹麦和挪威的收取贡赋的帝国。这些新领地很有价值：当时都柏林也许有4,000名居民，约克有10,000名，诺里奇有4,000名，伦敦有25,000名，远大于任何斯堪的纳维亚城镇。约克是与斯堪的纳维亚联系的重要纽带，伦敦则是与世界其余部分的纽带。这些岛屿虽然并未真正被城市网络纵横交错地覆盖，却与欧洲大陆的城市联系良好。

As other Scandinavians sailed out to Iceland, Greenland, and America, Canute and his raiders brought England temporarily into a tribute-taking empire that stretched to Denmark and Norway. The new domains were valuable: at that point, Dublin had perhaps 4,000 inhabitants, York 10,000, Norwich 4,000, and London 25,000, far larger than any Scandinavian town. York served as an important link to Scandinavia, and London to the rest of the world. While not exactly criss-crossed with urban networks, the islands connected well with the cities of continental Europe.
仅仅六十年后，诺曼人（早先在高卢定居的维京武士的后裔）又组织了一次对不列颠的入侵。他们对英格兰的征服遵循了那种典型模式：把土地作为封地分给士兵，而士兵由此成为王室的地区代理人（以及潜在的对手）。它减缓了斯堪的纳维亚人的入侵，并开启了英格兰统治者在不列颠之内和之外扩张其领地的进程。在接下来的两个世纪里，诺曼-英格兰和苏格兰的武力实际上把丹麦人和挪威人逐出了不列颠群岛的领土控制。

Only sixty years later, Normans (descendants of earlier Viking warriors who had settled in Gaul) organized one more invasion of Britain. Their conquest of England followed the characteristic pattern of distributing land in fief to soldiers become regional agents (and potential rivals) of the crown. It slowed Scandinavian incursions and started the process by which the rulers of England expanded their domains both within and beyond Britain. Over the next two centuries, Norman-English and Scottish arms practically eliminated Danes and Norwegians from control of territory in the British Isles.

随着联盟与继承的作用增加了在后来成为法国的地区内的“英格兰”属地，英格兰的统治者开始与其诺曼表亲交战。在12世纪，他们还试图把统治扩展到威尔士、苏格兰和爱尔兰。1152年与阿基坦的埃莉诺结婚后，亨利二世对统治英格兰、诺曼底、曼恩、布列塔尼、安茹、阿基坦和威尔士大部分地区拥有强有力的主张；在此后若干年里，他又把这些主张扩展到苏格兰和爱尔兰的部分地区。在治理那个帝国的过程中，他建立起一套相对有效的王室司法结构。然而从1173年起，他的儿子们开始与众多男爵、有时还与王后结盟，争夺他的权力。

As the play of alliance and inheritance increased "English" holdings in what was to become France, the rulers of England began warring with their Norman cousins. During the twelfth century, they also attempted to extend their rule to Wales, Scotland, and Ireland. With his marriage to Eleanor of Aquitaine in 1152, Henry II had strong claims to rule England, Normandy, Maine, Brittany, Anjou, Aquitaine, and much of Wales; during the following years, he extended those claims to Scotland and portions of Ireland. As he ran that empire, he built up a relatively effective royal judicial structure. Yet from 1173 onward his sons began to contest his power in alliance with many barons and, at times, the queen.

在战争制造和干预王朝争斗的过程中，英格兰国王们所倚以作战的男爵们获得了足够的权力，既能彼此交战，也能与国王交战，并迫使君主作出特许的让步——最戏剧性的便是《大宪章》。1215年的《大宪章》使国王承诺不再通过苛索封建义务来筹措战争资源，不再在男爵们不愿作战时雇用雇佣兵，并且只有经代表大贵族的大议事会同意才征收主要税项。议事会开始行使持久的权力，尤其因它在批准新税方面的地位而得到加强。后来的国王屡次确认该宪章。尽管如此，英格兰君主们持续不断地创建武装力量的努力，还是产生了一个持久的中央结构：王室国库、法院和领地。

In the process of making war and intervening in dynastic rivalries, the barons on whom English kings relied for their wars acquired enough power to fight the king as well as each other, exacting chartered concessions - most dramatically in Magna Carta - from the monarch. The Great Charter of 1215 committed the king to cease squeezing feudal obligations for the wherewithal to conduct wars, to stop hiring mercenaries when barons would not fight, and to impose the major taxes only with the consent of the great council, representative of the magnates. The council started to wield durable power, reinforced especially by its place in the approval of new taxation. Later kings confirmed the charter repeatedly. Nevertheless, the continuing efforts of English monarchs to create armed force produced a durable central structure: royal treasury, courts, and domain.

例如，爱德华一世（1272—1307）把强制骑士身份扩展到所有拥有年值二十英镑土地的人，要求所有骑士在王室民兵中服役，确立了为支付步兵薪饷而征收的税项，对羊毛和兽皮征收首批常规关税，建立起一支常设的中央班子，接管了此前由男爵和国王私人随从承担的一些活动，并使由男爵、郡骑士、市镇代表和教士分别组成、向他拨款的各个会议常规化。（1294年，为筹备在法国的又一次军事行动，爱德华甚至把羊毛出口税提高到六倍，并要求以税收形式取得教士收入的一半：Miller 1975: 11-12。）中央国家结构的创设在14世纪继续进行：不仅王室法院把其管辖权扩展到全国各地，而且治安法官开始作为王室的委任代理人行使地方权力。

Edward I (1272-1307), for example, extended compulsory knighthood to all holders of lands worth twenty pounds a year, required all knights to serve in royal militias, established taxation for the payment of foot soldiers, imposed the first regular customs dues on wool and hides, built up a permanent central staff who took over some of the activities previously performed by barons and the king's personal retainers, and regularized the separate assemblies of barons, knights of the shire, burgesses, and clergy that granted him money. (In 1294, preparing for another campaign in France, Edward went so far as to sextuple the export duty on wool and demand half the clergy's income in taxes: Miller 1975: 11- 12.) The creation of central state structure continued during the fourteenth century: not only did royal courts extend their jurisdiction throughout the land, but justices of the peace began to wield local power as commissioned agents of the crown.

这并不是说中心地带就稳定无虞。毕竟，爱德华二世死于狱中，是被谋杀的（1327）；爱德华三世去世时实际上已无权力（1377）；被废黜的理查二世死在狱中——或许也是被谋杀的（1400）。兰开斯特家族和约克家族为争夺王位进行了三十年内战（玫瑰战争，1455—85）；战争以理查三世被亨利·都铎的军队杀死而告终，后者随即成为亨利七世。围绕王权和王位继承的武装斗争持续了三个世纪，直到1688年光荣革命把奥兰治家族扶上王位。

Not that stability prevailed at the center. After all, Edward II died, murdered, in prison (1327), Edward III expired practically powerless (1377), and a deposed Richard II died - perhaps murdered as well - in prison (1400). The houses of Lancaster and York fought thirty years of civil war (the Wars of the Roses, 1455-85) over the right to the crown; the wars ended with Richard III slain by the forces of Henry Tudor, who thereupon became Henry VII. Armed struggles over royal power and royal succession continued for three centuries, until the Glorious Revolution of 1688 set the House of Orange on the throne.

与此同时，英格兰国王们一再试图夺取爱尔兰、威尔士、苏格兰和法国的领土。爱德华一世使威尔士屈服，并在名义上使爱尔兰和苏格兰臣属于英格兰王权。威尔士人此后只发动过一次严重的起义，即欧文·格伦道尔起义（1400—9）。然而，爱尔兰人和苏格兰人都顽强抵抗英格兰的统治，并常常得到法国国王的支持——后者乐于看到其英格兰对手被不列颠群岛内部的军事活动所牵制。在抵抗过程中，二者都创建了与英格兰对应机构有某些相似之处的议会。二者也都经历了围绕王位继承以及国王与男爵相对权力的血腥内部斗争。爱尔兰仍旧是一块难以驾驭的殖民地，而苏格兰则凭自身力量成为一个独立的欧洲强国。直到17世纪，爱尔兰和苏格兰才屈服于相对稳定的英格兰控制。

At the same time, English kings tried repeatedly to capture territory in Ireland, Wales, Scotland, and France. Edward I reduced Wales to subjugation as well as nominally subordinating Ireland and Scotland to the English crown. Welshmen only mounted one more serious rising, that of Owen Glendower (1400-9). Both Irish and Scots, however, resisted English rule tenaciously, and often found support from French kings who were happy to see their English rivals distracted by military activity within the British Isles. In the course of resistance both created parliaments having some parallels to their English counterpart. Both also experienced bloody internal struggles over royal succession and over the relative powers of kings and barons. While Ireland remained a fractious colony, Scotland became an independent European power in its own right. Not until the seventeenth century did Ireland and Scotland succumb to relatively stable English control.
英格兰国王为保住其在法国的领地而进行的长期（最终失败的）努力，使国家在1337年至1453年的大部分年份里处于战争状态。这一努力（后来被称为百年战争）的财政需求巩固了议会的地位，并使其两院的划分常规化。此后一个多世纪里，对苏格兰和法国的战争（有时是同时对二者）使议会参与王室的筹款，并确立了它同意征税的权利。

The long, and ultimately losing, effort of English kings to hold their French possessions kept the state at war through most of the years from 1337 to 1453. The financial demands of that effort (later called the Hundred Years' War) consolidated the position of Parliament, and regularized the division between its two houses. For well over a century thereafter, wars against Scotland and France (and sometimes both together) involved Parliament in royal fundraising, and established its right to consent to taxation.

下院——最终被称为平民院——聚集了自治市和郡的代表，其中自治市代表大多是商人，郡代表大多是地主。商人与地主之间一种漫长（尽管并不安稳）的联盟始于13世纪，当时不列颠的羊毛先是供应大陆的纺织制造业，随后又成为不列颠纺纱和织造的基础。不列颠开始了从出口羊毛到制造并出口毛织品的缓慢而命运攸关的转变。自那时起，英格兰商人在佛兰德立足，并开始向欧洲其余地区扩散。在15世纪，英格兰人同样证明自己是令人敬畏的航海者；例如，东海岸的水手在1412年前后重新开通了大陆与冰岛的贸易（Scammell 1981: 460）。1496年的商业条约《大通商条约》（Intercursus Magnus）使英格兰成为佛兰德国际贸易中被承认的伙伴。尽管外国商人和船只又支配了英格兰贸易半个世纪，但到1600年，英格兰人已在世界各地与西班牙人、葡萄牙人和荷兰人竞争。

The lower house, eventually to be called the Commons, assembled representatives of the boroughs and the counties, who were largely merchants on the one hand and landlords on the other. A long, if uneasy, alliance between merchants and landlords began in the thirteenth century, as British wool first fed continental textile manufactures and then became the basis for spinning and weaving in Britain. Britain began the slow but fateful shift from exporting wool to manufacturing and exporting woolens. From that point on, English merchants established themselves in Flanders, and began to spread out through the rest of Europe. During the fifteenth century, the English likewise proved themselves formidable men of the sea; east coast sailors, for example, reopened the continent's trade with Iceland around 1412 (Scammell 1981: 460). The Intercursus Magnus, a commercial treaty of 1496, established England as a recognized partner in Flemish international trade. Although foreign merchants and vessels dominated England's trade for another half-century, by 1600 the English were competing with Spaniards, Portuguese, and Dutchmen throughout the world.

在同一时期，不列颠的航海者——例如随约翰·卡伯特（他本人恰好是威尼斯人）航行的布里斯托尔人——开始加入荷兰人、意大利人、西班牙人和葡萄牙人的行列，探索世界的遥远地区，并为建立一个世界范围的贸易帝国奠定基础。到1577年，弗朗西斯·德雷克爵士正在环球航行。王室参与这些冒险，其限度在于它们有望增加政府收入或军事力量（Andrews 1984: 14-15）。不列颠地主在得到法律认可的圈占敞田和公地的帮助下，大量参与羊毛和谷物的交易；平民院日益代表商人与经济作物地主的紧密联盟。该国不断增长的商业实力促进了国家权力的增长；它使亨利七世（1484—1509）和后来的都铎诸王得以遏制苏格兰人、挑战法国人、扩展国家的战争制造权力、扩大征税，并削减大领主的私人军队。

In the same period, British seafarers such as the Bristol men who sailed with John Cabot (himself, as it happens, a Venetian) began joining Dutchmen, Italians, Spaniards, and Portuguese in exploring distant parts of the world, and in laying the bases for a world-wide trading empire. By 1577 Sir Francis Drake was circumnavigating the globe. The crown participated in these adventures to the extent that they promised additions to governmental revenues or military power (Andrews 1984: 14-15). British landlords, aided by legally sanctioned enclosures of open fields and common lands, involved themselves heavily in the marketing of wool and grain; the House of Commons came increasingly to represent a tight alliance of merchants and cash-cropping landowners. The country's growing commercial strength facilitated a growth in state power; it enabled Henry VII (1484-1509) and the later Tudors to check the Scots and challenge the French, expand the state's warmaking powers, extend taxation, and reduce the great lords' private armies.

亨利八世脱离罗马、夺取教会收入并没收修道院财产（1534—9），增加了王室收入，并使合作的教士与王室利益保持一致。都铎的扩张也激起了多次地区性叛乱，包括1536年的“恩典朝圣”大起义。尽管如此，都铎诸王最终还是遏制了拥有私人军队、声称拥有自主权力的大贵族（Stone 1965: 199-270）。该国几乎不停歇的商业化、无产阶级化和经济扩张，为国家活动提供了经济基础；而国家对关税和消费税的依赖，使从这一基础中抽取资源更为高效——但只有在显贵、王室和议会能够讨价还价达成合作协定时才是如此。

Henry VIII's secession from Rome, seizure of church revenues, and expropriation of monasteries (1534-9) enhanced royal revenues and aligned the cooperating clergy with royal interests. Tudor aggrandizement also incited repeated regional rebellions, including the great Pilgrimage of Grace (1536). Nevertheless the Tudors eventually curbed the great aristocrats, with their private armies and claims to autonomous power (Stone 1965: 199-270). The country's nearly ceaseless commercialization, proletarianization, and economic expansion provided an economic base for state activity, and the state's reliance on customs and excise made extraction of resources from that base more efficient - but only when magnates, crown, and Parliament could bargain out an agreement to cooperate.

在16世纪，苏格兰与法国日益接近；当年轻的苏格兰女王玛丽也成为法国王后时（1559），两个王国几近合并。但随后一场新教叛乱在苏格兰遏制了玛丽的权力；她在那里不稳固地统治了六年，随后又煽动了一场叛乱，并逃往英格兰接受伊丽莎白的保护性监禁；1586年她被斩首，结束了苏格兰受法国控制以及英格兰出现一位天主教女王的威胁。然而在伊丽莎白去世时，玛丽之子詹姆斯——他自1567年起即为苏格兰的詹姆斯六世——继承了英格兰王位，成为詹姆斯一世。与法国的联系几乎已经消散。

During the sixteenth century, Scotland drew ever closer to France; when the young Mary Queen of Scots became queen of France as well (1559), the two kingdoms approached merger. But a Protestant rebellion then contained Mary's power in Scotland, where she ruled unsteadily for six years before inciting another insurrection and fleeing to protective detention by Elizabeth in England; her beheading in 1586 ended the threat of a French Scotland and of a Catholic queen of England. At Elizabeth's death, however, Mary's son James, who had been James VI of Scotland since 1567, succeeded to the crown of England as James I. The French connection had almost dissolved.

在詹姆斯一世（1603—25）和后来的斯图亚特诸王治下，英格兰内部围绕为大陆战争筹措王室收入的斗争，引发了重大的宪政分裂、国王不经议会而统治（尤其是征税）的企图，最终导致一场处死查理一世的内战。作为时代的征兆，查理在1627年把最后一批王室领地转让给伦敦城，以此换得旧债的取消和一笔进一步的贷款；自此以后，他便陷入了信用危机，而他索要贷款和税收的要求只会加剧与议会及其金融家的冲突。到1640年，他夺取了存放在伦敦塔中保管的金银，并与拥有这些金银的金匠和商人讨价还价，以关税收入为担保借取贷款（Kindleberger 1984: 51）。查理试图招募并控制一支军队，以镇压爱尔兰的叛乱和苏格兰的抵抗，这使他自取灭亡。在共和国和护国政体时期（1649—60），军队和议会的各种不同派系统治着这个国家，同时试图把爱尔兰和苏格兰重新纳入国家控制，并与西班牙和荷兰交战。复辟由军队授意的议会邀请查理二世而启动，它确认了议会在不列颠国家之内的权力，尤其是在收入和支出方面。随着斯图亚特王朝的复辟，王室事务与大陆战争的紧密相互依赖继续下去，因为英格兰继续在海上与荷兰作战。1688年革命带来了联盟关系戏剧性的逆转；它把荷兰新教徒奥兰治的威廉及其妻子、约克公爵之女玛丽送上王位，而法国的路易十四则支持流亡的斯图亚特家族。此时不列颠恢复了其与法国的历史性竞争，并在此过程中借用了荷兰的制度。国家于1694年创立英格兰银行，作为为1688年开始的对法战争融资的工具（Kindleberger 1984: 52-3）。随着革命的结束和不列颠在欧洲大陆军事参与的恢复，一个新时代开始了。不列颠开始组建一支可观的常备军，一个有效的中央官僚机构成形，而批准税收的平民院相对于国王及其大臣获得了权力（Brewer 1989）。

Under James I (1603-25) and the later Stuarts, struggles within England over royal revenues for continental wars precipitated great constitutional divisions, attempts of kings to rule (and, especially, to tax) without Parliament, and eventually a civil war entailing execution of Charles I. In a sign of the times, Charles alienated the last block of crown lands to the City of London in 1627, receiving for it a cancellation of past debts and a further loan; from that point onward his credit failed, and his demands for loans and taxes only sharpened conflict with Parliament and its financiers. By 1640 he was seizing the gold and silver left in the Tower of London for safekeeping, and bargaining with the goldsmiths and merchants who owned it for a loan secured by customs revenues (Kindleberger 1984: 51). Charles' attempt to raise and control an army to put down rebellion in Ireland and resistance in Scotland did him in. During the Commonwealth and Protectorate (1649-60), varying fragments of the army and of Parliament ruled the country while trying to bring Ireland and Scotland back under state control and to battle against Spain and Holland as well. The Restoration, initiated by an army-inspired Parliamentary invitation to Charles II, confirmed the power of Parliament within the British state, especially when it came to revenues and expenditures. The tight interdependence of royal affairs and continental wars continued with the Stuart restoration, as England continued to fight Holland on the seas. The 1688 revolution brought a dramatic reversal of alliances; it carried Dutch Protestant William of Orange and his wife Mary, daughter of the duke of York, to the throne, as France's Louis XIV supported the exiled Stuarts. At that point Britain reverted to its historic rivalry with France, and borrowed Dutch institutions in the process. The state founded the Bank of England in 1694 as a vehicle for financing the war with France that had begun in 1688, (Kindleberger 1984: 52-3). With the end of revolution and the renewal of British military involvement on the Continent, a new era began. Britain started to form a substantial standing army, an effective central bureaucracy took shape, and the tax-granting House of Commons gained power vis-a-vis the king and his ministers (Brewer 1989).

苏格兰和爱尔兰一再发生的叛乱——常常涉及争夺英格兰王位的对手，更不用说法国在背后巧妙插手——又一次使国家的战争制造能力吃紧。战争与王朝斗争结合起来，造成了国家的重大变革，包括英格兰与苏格兰的稳固联合（1707）、德意志汉诺威家族（后来改称温莎）最终稳固地登上王位（1714—15），以及君主制与一个代表该国地产和商业利益的强大议会之间达成权宜共存（modus vivendi）。为斯图亚特王位觊觎者而发动的一场叛乱（1715）彻底失败，1745年的第二次叛乱也是如此，后者标志着对大不列颠王位继承的最后一次严重威胁。不列颠的军事力量持续增长：“到1714年，英国海军已是欧洲最庞大的海军，它雇用的工人比该国任何其他行业都多”（Plumb 1967: 119）。

Once again repeated rebellions in Scotland and Ireland - often involving rival claimants to the English crown, not to mention the fine hand of France - strained the state's warmaking powers. Wars and dynastic struggles combined to produce great transformations of the state, including a stable union of England with Scotland (1707), the definitive seating of the German house of Hanover (later renamed Windsor) on the throne (1714-15), and the establishment of a
modus vivendi

between the monarchy and a powerful Parliament representing the country's landed and commercial interests. A rebellion on behalf of the Stuart claimant to the throne (1715) failed utterly, as did a second rebellion in 1745, which marked the last serious threat to royal succession in Great Britain. British military power kept on growing: "By 1714, the British Navy was the largest in Europe, and it employed more workers than any other industry in the country" (Plumb 1967: 119).

与其大陆邻国相比，不列颠国家依靠相对较小的中央机构进行统治，并以一个庞大的庇护和地方权力持有体系为补充：在这个体系中，郡督、郡长、市长、治安官和治安法官为王室做事，却不作为其全职雇员；在拿破仑战争之前，只有关税和消费税部门拥有大量定期任命的官员。在此之前，不列颠不维持常备军，其武装力量尤其依赖战时对海上力量的动员。除爱尔兰之外，军队在控制不列颠国内人口方面所起的作用相对较小，民兵的作用则相对较大。在爱尔兰，英国政府在其整个霸权时期一直部署武装力量，并试验新的治安手段；事实上，不列颠通常把爱尔兰用作治安技术的试验场，这些技术后来被引入英格兰、威尔士和苏格兰（Palmer 1988）。

As compared with its continental neighbors, the British state governed by means of a relatively small central apparatus, supplemented by a vast system of patronage and local powerholding in which Lords Lieutenant, sheriffs, mayors, constables and justices of the peace did the crown's work without serving as its full-time employees; before the Napoleonic Wars, only customs and excise had substantial numbers of regularly appointed officials. Until then, Britain did not maintain a standing army, and relied especially on wartime mobilization of naval power for its armed force. Except in Ireland, the army played a relatively small part, and militias a relatively large part, in control of Britain's domestic population. In Ireland, the British government continued to deploy armed force and experiment with new means of policing throughout its time of hegemony; indeed, Britain generally used Ireland as a proving ground for techniques of policing the state later introduced in England, Wales, and Scotland (Palmer 1988).

大不列颠继续在欧洲作战，并在世界其余地方谋求帝国；对法七年战争结束（1763）时，不列颠成为世界上最强大的殖民国家。失去美洲殖民地（1776—83）并未像此前的失败那样威胁到国家权力。为对法作战而进行的反复动员，尤其是1793年至1815年间的动员，极大地扩大了税收、国债和国家对经济的干预，同时造成了影响从国王及其大臣向议会的一种微妙而决定性的转移。在那些战争期间（1801），大不列颠把爱尔兰并入联合王国（并非永久，但延续了一个多世纪）。到19世纪初，这个联合王国已成为由地主、金融家和商人支配的议会君主制的典范。

Great Britain kept on making war in Europe and striving for empire in the rest of the world; the end of the Seven Years' War against France (1763) left Britain the world's greatest colonial power. The loss of American colonies (1776-83) did not threaten state power in the way that previous defeats had. Repeated mobilizations for war with France, especially between 1793 and 1815, greatly expanded taxation, national debt, and state intervention in the economy, while causing a subtle but definitive shift in influence from the king and his ministers to Parliament. During those wars (1801), Great Britain incorporated Ireland (not definitively, but for more than a century) into a United Kingdom. By the early nineteenth century that United Kingdom had become the very model of a parliamentary monarchy dominated by landlords, financiers, and merchants.

帝国扩张贯穿了19世纪迅速的工业化和城市化。在不列颠内部，国家决定性地转向直接干预地方事务：在此前几个世纪里，国王和议会常常立法管制食品销售、集体行动的控制、穷人的待遇或工人的权利与义务，但他们几乎总是依靠地方当局来主动发起和执行。尽管不列颠维持地方当局的程度高于其许多大陆邻国，但在19世纪，国家官员前所未有地介入治安、教育、工厂检查、劳资冲突、住房、公共卫生以及广泛的其他事务。英国国家逐步地、却又决定性地走向直接统治。

Imperial expansion continued through the rapid industrialization and urbanization of the nineteenth century. Within Britain the state made a decisive shift toward direct intervention in local affairs: while in previous centuries king and parliament had frequently enacted legislation to govern the sale of food, the control of collective action, the treatment of the poor, or the rights and obligations of workers, they had almost always relied on local authorities for initiative and enforcement. While Britain maintained local authorities to a larger degree than many of its continental neighbors, during the nineteenth century national officials involved themselves as never before in policing, education, factory inspection, industrial conflict, housing, public health, and a wide range of other affairs. Incrementally but decisively, the British state moved toward direct rule.
尽管民族情绪偶尔被动员起来，威尔士和苏格兰早已不再威胁不列颠国家的分裂。但不列颠从未成功地整合、甚至从未成功地慑服爱尔兰的大部分地区。爱尔兰的抵抗和叛乱在第一次世界大战之后达到顶峰；经过若干步骤，除了新教色彩更重、更为英格兰化的东北角（阿尔斯特）之外，其余地区都成为一个独立国家，先是在英联邦之内，最终则在英联邦之外。阿尔斯特内部及围绕阿尔斯特的斗争至今没有结束。

Despite occasional mobilization of national sentiment, Wales and Scotland had long since ceased threatening the breakup of the British state. But Britain never succeeded in integrating, or even cowing, most of Ireland. Irish resistance and rebellion peaked in the aftermath of World War I; through several steps all but the more heavily Protestant and anglicized northeast corner (Ulster) became an independent state, first within the British Commonwealth, then finally outside it. The struggle in and over Ulster has not ended.

尽管在回顾中，大不列颠常常被当作政治稳定的典范，但仔细考察不列颠群岛的国家形成就会发现：强有力的各派如何不间断地争夺对国家的控制，以及从一个政体向下一个政体的过渡如何频繁地以暴力方式发生。爱尔兰的经历表明，该地区有能力沿着强制密集型路径创造一个相对弱小的国家。尽管如此，不列颠国家在18世纪和19世纪支配了世界的大部分地区，至今仍是一个世界强国。这个国家的历史并不简单地是威尼斯与俄罗斯、强制密集型国家与资本密集型国家历史之间的折中（甚至也不是综合）。

Although in retrospect Great Britain often serves as a model of political stability, a close look at state formation in the British Isles shows how continuously powerful parties battled for control of the state, and how often the transition from one regime to the next occurred in violence. Ireland's experience demonstrates the capacity of the region to create a relatively weak state along a coercion-intensive path. Nevertheless the British state came to dominate much of the world during the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, and remains a world power today. The history of that state is not simply a compromise (or even a synthesis) between the histories of Venice and Russia, of coercion-intensive and capital-intensive countries.

英格兰的、然后是英国的国家，建立在资本与强制的结合之上，这种结合很早就使任何君主都能获得巨大的战争制造手段，但代价是向该国的商人和银行家作出巨大让步。地主与商人之间不安稳的联盟制约了王室的自主性，却增强了国家权力。商业化的农业、远距离贸易、帝国征服和与欧洲对手的战争相互补充，促进了对海上力量的投资，以及为海外行动动员陆军的准备。城市和乡村经济的双重商业化意味着，为战争征税和借款比许多其他欧洲国家更容易，所需的国家机构也更少。亚当·斯密用英格兰与法国的简单比较来说明这一点。他写道：“在英格兰，政府所在地是世界上最大的商业城市，因此商人们一般就是向政府垫款的人……在法国，政府所在地不是一座大商业城市，因此在向政府垫款的人中，商人所占的比例就没有那么大”（Smith 1910 [1778]: II, 401）。在这一点上，英格兰比法国更接近资本密集型的国家形成路径。英格兰实现了这样一种非凡的结合：既有获取资本的便利，又严重依赖地主来承担王国的日常治理。尽管革命前的法国同样依赖贵族和教士承担其大部分地方政府职能，但从一个资本化和商业化程度较低的经济中榨取战争手段的努力，却建立起比英格兰臃肿得多的中央国家机构。

The English, then British, state built on a conjunction of capital and coercion that from very early on gave any monarch access to immense means of warmaking, but only at the price of large concessions to the country's merchants and bankers. The uneasy alliance between landlords and merchants constrained royal autonomy, but fortified state power. Commercialized agriculture, far-ranging trade, imperial conquest, and war against rival European powers complemented each other, promoting an investment in naval power and a readiness to mobilize land forces for action overseas. The commercialization of both urban and rural economies meant that taxation and borrowing for war went more easily, and with less state apparatus, than in many other European countries. Adam Smith put it in terms of a simple comparison between England and France. "In England," he remarked, "the seat of government being in the greatest mercantile city in the world, the merchants are generally the people who advance money to government ... In France, the seat of government not being in a great mercantile city, merchants do not make so great a proportion of the people who advance money to government" (Smith 1910 [1778]: II, 401). At that point England stood closer to the capital-intensive path of state formation than did France. England wrought a remarkable combination of easy access to capital and heavy reliance on landlords for day-to-day government of the realm. Although pre-revolutionary France relied similarly on nobles and priests for much of its local government, the effort to wring the means of war from a less capitalized and commercialized economy built up a significantly bulkier central state apparatus than in England.

然而，如果我们把威尼斯或莫斯科纳入考虑，就会立刻看到不列颠与法国的资本—强制关系极为相似。我们习惯于把不列颠、法国、普鲁士和西班牙的轨迹作为国家形成的主要替代类型加以对照。然而在整个欧洲范围之内，这四者具有共同属性，使它们明显区别于资本密集型路径和强制密集型路径。在四个例子中，雄心勃勃的君主都在16、17世纪军事力量积聚期间试图摧毁或绕过诸如各省等级会议之类的代议机构，成效不一；在法国和普鲁士，等级会议屈服了；在西班牙，议会（Cortes）蹒跚前行；在不列颠，议会作为统治阶级权力的堡垒存续了下来。在四个例子中，强制中心与资本中心的叠合——至少在一段时间内——促成了大规模军事力量的创建，而当时庞大、昂贵、装备精良的陆军和海军，使那些能够创建它们的民族国家在谋求霸权和帝国的过程中获得了压倒性优势。

Yet if we consider Venice or Moscow we immediately see great resemblances between capital-coercion relations in Britain and France. We are accustomed to contrasting the trajectories of Britain, France, Prussia, and Spain as the chief alternative types of state formation. Within the whole European range, however, the four have common properties that distinguish them clearly from the capital-intensive and coercion-intensive paths. In all four cases ambitious monarchs tried, with varying success, to crush or circumvent representative assemblies such as provincial Estates during the sixteenth- and seventeenth-century buildup of military power; in France and Prussia, the Estates succumbed, in Spain the Cortes staggered on, and in Britain Parliament survived as the bulwark of ruling-class power. In all four cases the coincidence of coercive centers with centers of capital facilitated - at least for a while - the creation of massive military force in a time when large, expensive, well-armed armies and navies gave those national states that were able to create them the overwhelming advantage in the search for hegemony and empire.

为什么威尼斯或俄罗斯没有变成英格兰？这个问题并不荒谬；它来自这样一种认识：欧洲国家总体上都在走向更大程度的资本集中和强制集中，向民族国家趋同。答案的一部分是：它们确实变得像英格兰了。参加第一次世界大战的俄罗斯国家和意大利国家，比其一个或两个世纪前的前身拥有多得多的民族国家特征。但更为深刻的答案是，它们以往的历史纠缠着它们。威尼斯创建的国家屈从于一个商业贵族阶层的利益，而这个贵族阶层发现，其优势在于寻找欧洲商业体系的缝隙，而不是协作努力去建立庞大的、持久的军事力量。俄罗斯创建的国家由一位名义上的专制君主领导，却完全依赖地主的合作——这些地主自身的利益决定了要把农民的劳动及其产品扣留下来，不用于国家的目的——并依赖一个可以轻易消耗国家所产生的任何剩余的官僚机构。不同类型的革命——一场意大利复兴运动和一次布尔什维克的夺取政权——把威尼斯人和莫斯科人带入新的国家，这些国家日益类似于西欧的伟大民族国家。但即便是这些后继国家，也带有其先前身份的印记。

Why didn't Venice or Russia become England? The question is not absurd; it follows from the recognition that European states in general moved toward greater concentrations of capital and coercion, converging on the national state. Part of the answer is: they did. The Russian and Italian states that entered World War I had far more of the traits of national states than had their predecessors of a century of two before. But the more profound answer is that their previous histories haunted them. Venice created a state that bent to the interests of a mercantile patriciate, and that patriciate found its advantage in seeking out the interstices of the European commercial system rather than by collaborating in any effort to build up massive, durable military power. Russia created a state led by a supposed autocrat, but totally dependent on the cooperation of landlords whose own interests dictated a withholding of peasant labor and its products from the state's ends, and on a bureaucracy that could easily consume any surplus the state generated. Different kinds of revolution - a Risorgimento and a Bolshevik seizure of power - drew Venetians and Muscovites into new states that came increasingly to resemble the great national states of western Europe. But even the successor states bore marks of their previous identities.

因此，把动态变化纳入施坚雅关于中国的图式化描绘，便为理解欧洲的经验提供了敏锐的洞见。它帮助我们认识到：在欧洲各地，武装力量的建设及其组织后果，如何因资本与强制、“自下而上”与“自上而下”的剥削与支配体系、以及城市与国家各自的相对分量不同而有所差异。尽管所有国家都为战争和备战付出了重大努力，但除此共同点之外，它们的主导活动因其在资本与强制网络中的位置及其先前历史而各不相同。此外，即使是类似的活动，也因发生的地点和时间不同而留下不同的组织残留。然而，与其他国家的关系越来越决定任何特定国家的结构与活动。由于大型民族国家在把本国资源转化为国际战争胜利方面具有优势，它们取代了收取贡赋的帝国、联邦、城邦以及所有其他竞争者，成为欧洲占主导地位的政治实体，并成为国家形成的样板。这些国家最终界定了欧洲国家体系的特征，并率先把它扩展到整个世界。

G. William Skinner's schematic portrait of China, set into motion, thus provides keen insight into European experience. It helps us recognize how the construction of armed force and its organizational consequences varied from one section of Europe to another as a function of the relative weight of capital and coercion, of the "bottom-up" and "top-down" systems of exploitation and domination, of cities and states. Although all states devoted major efforts to war and preparation for war, beyond that commonality their predominant activities varied according to their positions in the networks of capital and coercion and their prior histories. Even similar activities, furthermore, laid down different organizational residues depending on where and when they occurred. Increasingly, however, relations to other states determined the structure and activity of any particular state. Because of their advantages in translating national resources into success in international war, large national states superseded tribute-taking empires, federations, city-states, and all their other competitors as the predominant European political entities, and as the models for state formation. Those states finally defined the character of the European state system and spearheaded its extension to the entire world.
